_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the single input file x20-rd-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or API was used.

hints.reason: AMAZON via the Kindle e-reader it makes; FIRE via the verb to kindle a fire (with a bonus echo of the Kindle Fire tablet).

pairs.pair_note: Excellent double meaning; the Kindle Fire tablet makes it click even harder.

hints.reason: SAIL is immediate (yachts sail), but AMERICA only arrives via the America's Cup yacht race, which YACHT alone does not strongly evoke for most players.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are accurate; the AMERICA side is a one-step-too-far link for a general audience.

hints.reason: BACK via the phrase arch your back; CAT via the classic image of a scared or stretching cat arching its back.
hints.fix: To arch your back is to bend it into a curve, as a scared cat does.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, familiar image; the BACK line's 'curve it upward' is confusing for humans, so a small wording fix is suggested.

hints.reason: BARBIE via Ryan Gosling playing Ken in the 2023 film; CHICK via a gosling being a baby goose, a young bird.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pop-culture plus animal double meaning with a real aha.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via a base hit; SONG via a hit single.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean classic double meaning.

hints.reason: BEACH via sandy beaches; SPONGEBOB via his squirrel friend Sandy Cheeks.

pairs.pair_note: Satisfying adjective-versus-character double meaning.

hints.reason: BIG via The Big Bang Theory, where Sheldon is a lead; YOUNG via the prequel Young Sheldon.

pairs.pair_note: Two title words tied by one character; clicks quickly and feels good.

hints.reason: BLOCK via sunblock and SCREEN via sunscreen, two instantly familiar compounds for the same product.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but the two compounds being near-synonyms makes it a neat pairing.

hints.reason: CLOUD via mushroom cloud and BOMB via the nuclear blast that famously produces one; both come from the same iconic image.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar and fair; subject matter is serious but PG-acceptable.

hints.reason: BRAIN via the creature's stolen brain (also the famous 'Abby Normal' brain gag); YOUNG via Mel Brooks's Young Frankenstein.
hints.fix: In the 1931 film, the doctor's assistant steals a brain from a medical college for the creature.

pairs.pair_note: Good route; the BRAIN line's 'stolen from a lab' is imprecise (Fritz takes it from a medical college lecture hall, and the doctor did not steal it himself).

hints.reason: BROWN via Doc Brown, who builds the DeLorean time machine; TIME via its time travel at 88 mph.

pairs.pair_note: Iconic film reference with a satisfying click.

hints.reason: BUSINESS via monkey business is instant, but FUNNY arrives only through the synonym chain monkey business = funny business (or monkeys being comic), which few players will reach from MONKEY alone.

pairs.pair_note: Cute equivalence once explained, but the FUNNY side is indirect and many other board words could also fit MONKEY.

hints.reason: WORM via gummy worms and CANDY via gummies being a chewy candy.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, instantly familiar; fine as a gentle clue.

hints.reason: CHARGE via a charging bull; CHINA via the idiom a bull in a china shop.

pairs.pair_note: Strong: an idiom plus a behaviour, and the CHINA side has a nice aha.

hints.reason: CHESS via checkmate (often just 'mate'); ROOM via roommate.

pairs.pair_note: Compounds, but the chess sense of mate makes it feel like a real double meaning.

hints.reason: FILM via flick being slang for a film; CHICK via the phrase chick flick.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym plus familiar phrase; honest on both sides.

hints.reason: CLOCK via the nursery rhyme Hickory Dickory Dock; SMOKE via hickory wood for smoking meat.

pairs.pair_note: Lovely pairing of a nursery rhyme and barbecue; real aha.

hints.reason: CLUB via the golf caddy who carries clubs; TEA via a tea caddy, a tin for loose tea.

pairs.pair_note: Tea caddy is less common in U.S. speech but widely enough known; a satisfying double meaning.

hints.reason: LIGHTNING via lightning rod is instant, but CONDUCTOR only connects through the technical fact that the rod conducts current; ROD does not bring a conductor (train or orchestra) to mind.

pairs.pair_note: Facts are true, but the CONDUCTOR side is a definition rather than a natural link; no obviously better one-word hint found.

hints.reason: COOL via the Cool Ranch flavour; TRIANGLE via the chips' triangular shape.

pairs.pair_note: Fun brand clue that clicks immediately.

hints.reason: COWBOY via cowboy boots; TRUNK via the familiar British word boot for a car trunk.

pairs.pair_note: The owner has explicitly cleared British 'boot'; british_only is a familiarity note only.

hints.reason: CROSS and FINGER together via the good-luck gesture of crossing your fingers.

pairs.pair_note: Simple and fair; both targets come from the same gesture.

hints.reason: DEAD via the band the Grateful Dead; THANKSGIVING via the holiday of being grateful.

pairs.pair_note: Band-name join, but the meaning link to Thanksgiving gives a genuine aha.

hints.reason: DISH via Petri dish; LAB via Petri dishes being a lab staple for growing cultures.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but tight; PETRI has no use outside the lab, so it is precise.

hints.reason: DOWN via crossword clues listed Across and Down; NEWSPAPER via the daily newspaper crossword.

pairs.pair_note: The DOWN side is a nice indirect aha.

hints.reason: END via French fin, the closing card of classic films; SHARK via its dorsal fin.

pairs.pair_note: Strong cross-language double meaning; 'fin' as 'the end' is widely known from films and cartoons.

hints.reason: FIELD via pitch meaning a playing field; SOCCER via the familiar phrase soccer pitch.

pairs.pair_note: Soccer pitch is well known in the U.S.; the baseball sense of pitch adds a fair misdirect.

hints.reason: WIZARD via Gandalf the wizard; FIREWORKS via his famous fireworks at Bilbo's party in the opening of The Fellowship of the Ring.

pairs.pair_note: The fireworks scene is prominent in book and film, so I lean PASS, but casual viewers may not recall it; a second opinion is welcome.

hints.reason: FULL via feeling stuffed after a meal; SCARECROW via being stuffed with straw.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning with a pleasant twist.

hints.reason: HAMBURGER via the burger patty; MINT via the peppermint patty candy.

pairs.pair_note: Savoury versus sweet patty; a real 'oh, nice'.

hints.reason: HOSPITAL via M*A*S*H, set at a Mobile Army Surgical Hospital; POTATO via mashed potatoes.

pairs.pair_note: An older show but still widely known; excellent double meaning.

hints.reason: JACK via author Jack London; WILD via his novel The Call of the Wild.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar literature link; the city misdirect makes it a nice solve.

hints.reason: PINK via the band name Pink Floyd; LASER via the band's famous laser light shows and the long-running planetarium Laser Floyd shows.

pairs.pair_note: Pink Floyd is instantly familiar and the laser-show association is real and fairly well known; the LASER side is the weaker half.

hints.reason: LIGHTNING via a lightning bolt; RECORD via Usain Bolt's sprint world records.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, and the lightning-bolt pose ties the two senses together neatly.

hints.reason: MEMORY via Dory's short-term memory loss; WHALE via her famous attempt to speak whale in Finding Nemo.

pairs.pair_note: Two iconic character traits; delightful.

hints.reason: MILK via skim milk; STONE via skimming stones across water.

pairs.pair_note: Americans more often say 'skip' stones, but 'skim' is understood; nice double meaning.

hints.reason: MOUSTACHE via the Pringles mascot Mr. P's big moustache; POTATO via Pringles being potato crisps.

pairs.pair_note: Fun brand clue; 'potato crisps' matches Pringles' own U.S. labelling.

hints.reason: OFFICE via the Oval Office; SHAPE via an oval being a shape.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, clean, and fair.

hints.reason: PUZZLE via jigsaw puzzle; PICTURE via the picture a jigsaw builds when completed.

pairs.pair_note: PICTURE side is a little softer but natural; easy clue.

hints.reason: POISON via poison hemlock (Socrates' death); TREE via the unrelated hemlock evergreen.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate text, including the note that the tree and the poison plant are unrelated.

hints.reason: SAFE via safecracker; SNACK via crackers as a snack.

pairs.pair_note: Satisfying double meaning.

hints.reason: SKIN and SNAKE together via snakes shedding their skin.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and clear.

hints.reason: STAFF via a shepherd's crook; THIEF via crook as slang for a criminal.

pairs.pair_note: The shepherd's-staff sense gives a real aha beyond the synonym.

hints.reason: WALK via The Walking Dead; ZOMBIE via zombies being the (un)dead that the show is about.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar title join reinforced by the zombie meaning.
